guidelines.title: Project Intent and Scope
guidelines.description: This is a personal, production-quality collection of small Python tools. The codebase prioritizes correctness, clarity, and minimalism over abstraction or extensibility. Changes should be narrowly scoped to the requested task.

guidelines.title: Python Standards
guidelines.description: Target Python 3.13+ exclusively. Do not add compatibility code for earlier Python versions. Prefer modern Python features and standard library APIs. Type annotations are expected for all non-trivial functions and public interfaces.

guidelines.title: Tooling Authority
guidelines.description: Use `uv` for dependency management and script execution. Use `ruff` for linting and formatting, `pyright` for static type analysis in strict mode, and `pytest` for testing. Configuration in `pyproject.toml` is authoritative.

guidelines.title: Dependency Policy
guidelines.description: Do not introduce new runtime or development dependencies without explicit permission. Prefer the Python standard library and existing project dependencies. If a new dependency appears necessary, ask for confirmation and justify its inclusion.

guidelines.title: Linting and Formatting Behavior
guidelines.description: Generated or modified code must comply with `ruff` linting and formatting rules. Do not reformat or restyle existing code unless it is directly related to the requested change.

guidelines.title: Type Checking Discipline
guidelines.description: All new or modified code must satisfy `pyright` strict type checking. Do not weaken type strictness or suppress type errors unless explicitly requested.

guidelines.title: Testing Requirements
guidelines.description: New behavior or bug fixes must be accompanied by appropriate tests in the `tests/` directory. Existing tests must not be weakened or removed without explicit instruction. Test changes should preserve or improve coverage and behavioral guarantees.

guidelines.title: Coverage Expectations
guidelines.description: Aim for at least 70% coverage for new and changed code unless explicitly instructed otherwise. If coverage would decrease due to a change, additional tests should be added unless explicitly instructed otherwise.

guidelines.title: Error Handling Strategy
guidelines.description: Prefer raising descriptive exceptions or allowing them to bubble up over returning `None`, error codes, or empty collections to signal failure. For CLI tools, catch exceptions at the entry point to provide clean user-facing error messages and appropriate exit codes. Do not suppress or swallow exceptions unless explicitly requested otherwise or when it is the intended semantic behavior of a narrow utility.

guidelines.title: Refactoring Boundaries
guidelines.description: Do not refactor existing implementation code unless it is necessary to fulfill the requested change. Avoid drive-by cleanups, architectural changes, or stylistic refactors. Prefer minimal, localized diffs.

guidelines.title: Testability Refactoring Constraint
guidelines.description: Do not refactor implementation code solely to improve testability if the refactoring would change non-test behavior, control flow, public interfaces, or observable semantics. If improved testability would require such changes, ask for explicit confirmation before proceeding.

guidelines.title: Docstring Standard
guidelines.description: Use Google-style docstrings for non-trivial public interfaces. Since type annotations are mandatory and enforced by pyright, do not repeat type information within the docstring. Focus purely on the semantic description of parameters and return values.

guidelines.title: Workflow
guidelines.description: Use the provided `Makefile` targets as the reference workflow (`make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test`, `make fmt`, `make all`). Generated changes should be compatible with these workflows without requiring additional steps.

guidelines.title: End of plan cleanliness
guidelines.description: Run `make fmt` and `make test` before completing a plan.  These must complete successfully without errors or warnings.  Stop and ask for direction if you are unable to satisfy this.  This rule defines completion requirements, not intermediate development steps.

guidelines.title: Ruff Compliance
guidelines.description: Ensure that all code adheres to the Ruff linting rules as specified in `pyproject.toml`.

guidelines.title: No init all
guidelines.description: In __init__.py: no re-exports, no __all__, modules are imported explicitly.

guidelines.title: Tests Must Not Be Python Packages
guidelines.description: The top-level tests directory MUST NOT be a Python package. The tests/ directory must not contain an __init__.py file. Tests are discovered and executed by pytest as plain modules and must import only from the installed project package, never from other test modules. Shared test functionality must be provided via conftest.py or explicit helper subpackages within tests/, not by making tests/ itself a package.
